## Repository findings

The repository is essentially a **scaffold, not an existing game or app**. Git tracks only the README and an OpenCode GitHub Actions workflow; there’s no frontend source, package manifest, or game code to extend.

- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/README.md` — identifies the project as an OMGithub-created project, but contains no app or implementation details.

**Framework:** Not established by the repository. The Pascal and WebGPU references suggest an expected external environment, but there’s no local app code or dependency manifest to confirm how to build on it.

## Recommended implementation

Treat “make an AI that can make 3D games” as a new product to build, rather than a modification to an existing game. First establish the app scaffold and framework supported by the runtime. Then build a creator interface with a natural-language prompt, an editable game/scene preview, and controls to regenerate or revise the result.

For game generation, prefer a constrained, typed game/scene specification over unrestricted generated code: turn the prompt into entities, materials, lighting, camera, environment, and basic gameplay rules, then render that specification in a 3D runtime. Add a prompt-to-spec step, validation and preview, and save/export support. The bundled Three.js/PlayCanvas skill may help with importing models, but the repository doesn’t currently include either engine as an application dependency.
